Implement upload/read features against the Data API within the default quota

approval.cost: No fee for verification or the audit is stated in the documentation read
approval.trigger: Two independent gates, neither an app-store review. (a) Google OAuth verification (identity/scope layer): while the consent screen is in Testing status, the app 'is only available to users you add to the list of test users'. Scopes are classified non-sensitive / sensitive / restricted, and 'Sensitive scopes require review by Google before any Google Account can grant access' (Google's own examples of sensitive scopes include 'deleting a YouTube video', which the YouTube write scopes cover). Verification requires declaring all scopes, a detailed justification per scope, and a demonstration video; brand verification is handled first (automated review 'usually completes in a few minutes'). An app in production with sensitive scopes before verification shows users the 'unverified app' warning screen and is subject to the 100-user cap until verified (per Google's OAuth App Verification Help Center). (b) YouTube API Services compliance audit (quota layer), NOT required to launch, only to exceed the default quota: 'Projects that enable the YouTube Data API have a default quota allocation of 100 search.list calls, 100 videos.insert calls, and 10,000 units per day combined for all other endpoints.' 'If you would like to request additional quota beyond the default allocation, you must first complete an audit to show that your project is in compliance with the YouTube API Services Terms of Service.' You submit the YouTube API Services Audit and Quota Extension Form; 'A member of YouTube's API Services team will contact you as soon as possible.' There are also dedicated Appeals, Periodic Audit, and Change of Control forms: audits recur, and a change of control of the project must be reported. No directory/marketplace listing exists.
approval.wait: Sensitive scope verification: 'typically takes 3-5 business days to complete' (stated). YouTube compliance audit: not stated

blockers.detail: In Testing status only listed test users can authorize AND refresh tokens die after 7 days ('A Google Cloud Platform project with an OAuth consent screen configured for an external user type and a publishing status of Testing is issued a refresh token expiring in 7 days', unless only basic profile scopes are requested). A SaaS that forgets to publish will see every connection break weekly.
blockers.howToClear: Move the consent screen to In production before real users connect, and complete verification for your sensitive scopes.
blockers.title: Testing-mode double trap

blockers.detail: You cannot buy quota; the default 10,000 units/day (plus the separate 100/day buckets for search.list and videos.insert) is all you get until a compliance audit passes, and there is no published audit SLA.
blockers.howToClear: Design within the default quota from the start and file the audit early if your product needs more.
blockers.title: Quota is the hard ceiling, and the audit is the only way through it

blockers.detail: Classifications appear when you declare scopes in the console; adding a new sensitive scope to a live, verified app re-triggers the unverified-app screen and the user cap until the new scope is approved. Google's guidance is to test new scopes in a separate project, and its policies require separate projects for testing and production anyway.
blockers.howToClear: Fix the scope set before verification and experiment in a separate project.
blockers.title: Verification is scope-driven and discovered late

flavor.recommended: A Web application OAuth client in a Google Cloud project, authorization code flow with access_type=offline and incremental authorization
flavor.why: There is no YouTube-specific app object. The object is a Google Cloud project containing an OAuth 2.0 client ID (Google API Console / Google Auth Platform) plus an OAuth consent screen configuration; the YouTube Data API is simply enabled on the project, and YouTube permissions are requested as Google OAuth scopes: youtube.readonly (view your YouTube account), youtube.upload (manage your YouTube videos), youtube (manage your YouTube account), youtube.force-ssl (see, edit, and permanently delete videos, ratings, comments and captions), youtube.channel-memberships.creator, youtubepartner, and youtubepartner-channel-audit. 'The refresh token is only returned if your application set the access_type parameter to offline.'

humanMust: Create/select a Google Cloud project and enable the YouTube Data API (separate projects for testing and production)
Configure the OAuth consent screen/branding (app name, logo, support email, developer contact, home page and privacy policy URLs, authorized domains verified in Search Console)
Create the Web application client and download client_secret.json
Declare scopes on the Data Access page; move the consent screen to In production; submit OAuth verification (per-scope justification + demo video) if your scopes require it
name: YouTube
nuances: Partial consent is normal: with granular permissions, users may grant only some scopes; 'your app must verify which scopes were actually granted' and disable features whose scopes were denied.

Refresh tokens generally: valid until the user revokes access or the token expires; a refresh token also stops working if it 'has not been used for six months' or if the account exceeds the token limit: 'There is currently a limit of 100 refresh tokens per Google Account per OAuth 2.0 client ID. If the limit is reached, creating a new refresh token automatically invalidates the oldest refresh token without warning.' No refresh token without access_type=offline; re-prompting consent (prompt=consent) is needed to reliably re-issue one.
Token size limits your storage must tolerate: authorization codes up to 256 bytes, access tokens up to 2048 bytes, refresh tokens up to 512 bytes.

Upload privacy: the videos resource reference currently states, for status.privacyStatus, that 'Videos uploaded from unverified API projects are not restricted to private viewing mode', i.e. as of this reading the docs do NOT impose a private-only lock on uploads from unverified projects (creator account settings can still default individual uploads to private).
prerequisites: A Google Cloud project with the YouTube Data API enabled
Consent-screen branding assets and verified authorized domains (Search Console)
A scope set fixed before verification, plus a demo video for sensitive-scope verification

steps.detail: Create/select a project and enable the YouTube Data API in the API Library. Google's OAuth policies require separate projects for testing and production.

links.label: Using OAuth 2.0 for Web Server Applications

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project; enable the YouTube Data API

steps.detail: App name, logo, support email, developer contact info, home page URL, privacy policy URL, authorized domains (domain ownership verified in Google Search Console). Then Clients page > Create Client > Web application, register authorized redirect URIs, download client_secret.json, and store it securely. Declare your scopes on the project's Data Access page (non-sensitive / sensitive / restricted, which determines whether verification is triggered).
steps.title: Configure the consent screen; create the client

steps.detail: Redirect the user to Google's authorization server with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, the YouTube scopes, state, and access_type=offline. Exchange the returned code server-side for an access token + refresh token; store the refresh token, and verify which scopes were actually granted (granular consent) before enabling features.
steps.title: Build the flow (access_type=offline)

steps.detail: Call the YouTube Data API with Authorization: Bearer; refresh the access token with the stored refresh token when it expires. Stay within the default quota (100 search.list calls, 100 videos.insert calls, 10,000 units per day for all other endpoints combined) unless an audit has granted more.
steps.title: Call the API; refresh

steps.detail: Move the consent screen publishing status from Testing to In production, and complete OAuth verification in the Cloud Console Verification Center if your scopes require it (per-scope justification and a demo video for sensitive scopes; brand verification first, automated review 'usually completes in a few minutes'; sensitive scope verification 'typically takes 3-5 business days').
steps.title: Publish and complete OAuth verification

steps.detail: Submit the YouTube API Services Audit and Quota Extension Form. 'A member of YouTube's API Services team will contact you as soon as possible' (no timeline stated). Reuse the same form for further extensions within 12 months of a passed audit; dedicated forms exist for Appeals, Periodic Audit, and Change of Control.
steps.title: (Only for more quota) Request the compliance audit

tagline: YouTube has no app object of its own: it is a Google Cloud OAuth client with YouTube scopes, gated by Google's sensitive-scope verification (typically 3 to 5 business days, with a 100-user cap while unverified) and by a separate YouTube compliance audit that is the only way past the default daily quota.
